Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Nepal's reply. The two umpires have made their way out to the middle as have the players of Bangladesh. It will be Aasif Sheikh and Kushal Bhurtel to open the innings for Nepal. Tanzim Hasan Sakib has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, this has all the makings of another low-scoring thriller. On a surface that has offered the most turn of any venue in this World Cup, it is not going to get any easier for Nepal. Bangladesh will back themselves to defend this total, knowing that a win will secure their spot in the Super 8s. If they lose and lose badly, the Netherlands will have a strong chance to advance, provided they win against Sri Lanka. Join us back in a bit for the second essay.

Sompal Kami is in for a chat. He says that the wicket was really good and he is happy to reap the rewards for his hard work and planning. Thanks the skipper, Rohit Paudel for believing in him and giving him 3rd over on the trot in the Powerplay. States that it is a slow wicket, which is why they wanted to use a spinner at the death. Shares that it is a tricky wicket and that they will have to bat sensibly to get over the line.

For Bangladesh, the match began disastrously with the loss of Tanzid Hasan on the first ball, and it only got worse from there. Attempting to take the game to Nepal, they were rocked early, losing 4 wickets in the Powerplay. The experienced duo of Shakib Al Hasan and Mahmudullah then joined forces to stabilize the innings. Just as they seemed to be rebuilding, a mix-up led to Mahmudullah's downfall. Things deteriorated further as Shakib also fell soon after without making a significant impact. Batting with the tail, Rishad Hossain got a couple of boundaries away but failed to bat through. Thanks to the last-wicket stand of 18 runs between Mustafizur Rahman and Taskin Ahmed, Bangladesh were able to scrap their way to 106.

A masterful bowling effort by Nepal to bowl Bangladesh out for 106. However, they will still feel that they gave 10 runs more than what it looked to be at one stage. After opting to bowl first, Nepal got off to a dream start. Sompal Kami set the tone by striking on the very first ball of the game. Building on that early breakthrough, Dipendra Singh Airee maintained the pressure, and Kami rewarded the skipper's decision to give him a third consecutive over. Towhid Hridoy showed some positive intent but his stay was cut short by Rohit Paudel, compounding Bangladesh's struggles. The Nepalese spinners then took over and chipped away at the wickets in the middle phase. However, the gamble to give Abinash Bohara the 19th over, instead of opting for a frontline bowler, may come back to haunt Nepal as he conceded 11 runs. This decision could prove crucial in such a tightly contested match.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Sompal Kami to Shakib Al Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! In complete control and Das finds the fence this time! Keeps it full and on off and middle, Litton Das gets inside the line and rolls his wrists to control the sweep. Hits it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Aerial but safe! Fuller and quicker, on off, Litton Das reaches out in front for the sweep but gets a top edge that lands safely, well away from deep backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! Slows it up and keeps it full as well, outside off, Litton Das springs on the front foot to go down the ground but connects with thin air.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tosses it up, full and on off, Litton Das lunges and knocks it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and on off, Litton Das punches it nicely but straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A big mix-up but Shakib Al Hasan gets away with it! A better throw and Shakib was nowhere in the frame. Short and on off, Shakib Al Hasan slaps it to backward point where Kushal Bhurtel dives to his right to make the stop. Shakib is caught ball-watching and he is late to set off but a wayward throw at the bowling end, allows Shakib to make his ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Dipendra Singh Airee to Shakib Al Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! At 132.6 kph, on a short of a good length, shaping away, in the channel on off, Litton Das pokes at the delivery and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Sompal Kami to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Little bit of away shape, on a length, outside off, Litton Das times the drive well but can't get it past cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Sompal Kami to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes wide of the crease on that around-the-wicket angle and lands it on a back of a length, on off, Shakib Al Hasan taps it with soft hands in front of cover and calls Das through for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Sompal Kami to Shakib Al Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls the heavy ball again does Kami, outside off, Shakib Al Hasan ducks and lets it go through to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Sompal Kami to Shakib Al Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dishes it out at 136 kph, honing in at the pads, on a short of a good length, Shakib Al Hasan tries to glance it away off the pads but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Sompal Kami to Shakib Al Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs it into the surface, on middle, Litton Das fails to ride the bounce as he looks to work it away on the leg side. Gets a leading edge that drops in the vacant mid-wicket region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Sompal Kami to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fires it in again but much fuller, on off, Shakib Al Hasan pushes it in front of cover to end a successful over for Nepal.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Dipendra Singh Airee to Shakib Al Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, the first sign of extra bounce! Pushes it through, on a nagging length, outside off, Shakib Al Hasan shapes up for the cut but the ball kicks off and sails over the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Dipendra Singh Airee to Shakib Al Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shakib Al Hasan is up and running! Dipendra Singh Airee floats it but offers width, slower as well, Shakib Al Hasan reaches out and creams the drive past covers for a boundary to get going.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Dipendra Singh Airee to Shakib Al Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Shakib Al Hasan walks out to bat now!

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Dipendra Singh Airee strikes in his first over too and Nepal could not have asked for a better start. This is the 18th time since the 2022 T20 World Cup that Najmul Hossain Shanto has fallen to off-spin. Airee slides it in with the angle, full and around off, Najmul Hossain Shanto presses forward and plays for the turn but there isn't any. The ball comes in with the arm, sneaks past the inside edge and rattles into the off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Dipendra Singh Airee to Najmul Hossain Shanto, OUT! b Dipendra Singh Airee.

Commentary.Commentary: Good effort in the deep! Airee drops it short and offers a bit of width, outside off, Litton Das rocks on the back foot and cuts it past point. Sompal Kami gives it a chase and dives full-length to pull the back in. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Dipendra Singh Airee to Litton Das, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts it flat and short, on off, Najmul Hossain Shanto goes on the back foot and clips it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Dipendra Singh Airee to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end then? Dipendra Singh Airee it is.

Given LBW but successfully overturned by Litton Das. Sompal Kami angled it into the right-hander from over the wicket, on a good length, around the pads, Litton Das plays all around it and gets beaten on the inside edge. Gets rapped on the front pad. Just a half a shout for LBW but up goes the finger.  Litton Das has a word with Najmul Hossain Shanto and takes the review. There is nothing on UltraEdge. The impact is umpire's call but the angle has taken the ball past the leg stump on Ball Tracking. Das survives an early scare.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Sompal Kami to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Gets a good away shape on this one and it is full as well, on off, Litton Das covers the line of the ball and defends it out with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Sompal Kami to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bends his back again does Kami and digs it in short, on middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto gets on his toes and nudges it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Sompal Kami to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Najmul Hossain Shanto and Bangladesh are away! Lands it on a shortish length, over middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto hops back and rolls his wrists to pull it wide of deep backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Sompal Kami to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes wide of the crease and slants it on a back of a length, on middle and leg, Najmul Hossain Shanto looks to work it away with the angle and gets beaten on the inside edge to get hit on the hips.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Sompal Kami to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! What a start for Sompal Kami and Nepal! Golden duck for Tanzid Hasan. Kami steams in from around the wicket and bangs it into the deck, angling in, on middle and leg, Tanzid Hasan premeditates and skips down the track to take the short ball on but gets cramped for room and the ball gets big on him. Hits the splice of the bat and lobs tamely to the left of Kami who makes no mistake. Najmul Hossain Shanto is the new man in.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Sompal Kami to Tanzid Hasan, OUT! c & b Sompal Kami.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the action to begin now. Litton Das and Tanzid Hasan are the openers. Sompal Kami to begin. Here we go...
Time for the National Anthems! Nepal will sing their first and then it will be Bangladesh's turn!

PITCH REPORT - Alan Wilkins is near the deck. He says that a nice breeze is blowing across the venue. Tells that it is a 68-metre boundary on one side and 61-metre to the other side with a 74-metre straight hit. Samuel Badree joins him and says that if you are a spinner, this is the venue where you want to be at. Further says that this venue has seen the highest degree of turn of all venues at this World Cup and spinners will enjoy themselves here. Informs that 19 wickets have fallen to spin at this ground while pacers have taken only 7 wickets. Badree shares that there are a few bare areas and the ball might behave differently from those areas. Adds that variable bounce will be challenging for the batters.
Bangladesh's skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto says he is very proud of the effort shown by the boys so far. Informs they have no changes.

The captain of Nepal, Rohit Paudel says that they will bowl first. Adds that with the dew coming in, it might get tough to bowl later. Says they are disappointed with the last result but are looking forward for this game. Mentions the fans have been very supportive and he wants to thank them. Informs they have one change with Sundeep Jora coming in for Karan KC.

Nepal (Playing XI) - Kushal Bhurtel, Aasif Sheikh, Anil Sah, Rohit Paudel(C), Kushal Malla, Sundeep Jora (In for Karan KC), Dipendra Singh Airee, Gulshan Jha, Sompal Kami, Sandeep Lamichhane, Abinash Bohara.

Bangladesh (Unchanged Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Litton Das (WK), Shakib Al Hasan, Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mustafizur Rahman.
TOSS - Nepal have won the toss and ELECTED TO BOWL!

On the other hand, Nepal will be looking to recover from their heartbreaking last-ball defeat and aim to finish on a high note. Their spin attack has been effective, and they will likely rely on it again in this game. With the bat, Nepal has the potential to dismantle opposition bowling attacks, but success will require a collective effort and the ability to withstand pressure, something they struggled with against South Africa. In the last game, Rohit Paudel and his men showed that they pack a punch and can challenge the top sides. Are we in for a late twist in Group D? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up.

Bangladesh, with 4 points from 3 games, are in the best position to advance and need just a point to secure their spot. The Netherlands, the other team in contention, are hoping for a heavy defeat for Bangladesh. If that happens, the Dutch will need to win big enough against Sri Lanka to surpass Bangladesh on NRR. Although Bangladesh's top order has struggled, their middle order has stepped up, compensating for the lack of runs at the top. Their pace attack has been impressive, and Najmul Hossain Shanto has also had his spin department deliver at crucial times.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the game between Bangladesh and Nepal at the Arnos Vale Ground in St. Vincent. As we reach the climax of Group D, with two games remaining, the race to join South Africa in the Super 8s is still open.
... MATCH DAY ...

The race for the last remaining Super 8 spot in Group D is heating up, and Nepal's heartbreaking 1-run loss against South Africa has left Bangladesh and the Netherlands as the two surviving contenders. Najmul Hossain Shanto and his men now face Nepal at the Arnos Vale Ground in St. Vincent. Nepal do not have much to lose from this game, but Bangladesh have everything to gain, as a win by any margin will suffice for them to go through. However, the Netherlands are in with an outside chance here, hoping for a Nepal win, and then they will need to beat Sri Lanka by a healthy enough margin to pip Bangladesh on NRR. It was a hard-fought win for Bangladesh in the last encounter against the Dutch, where the return to form for Shakib Al Hasan was the biggest positive for them. While Towhid Hridoy has shown glimpses of his potential, Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Mahmudullah, who haven't had the desired impact, will be required to step up. Leggie Rishad Hossain has been the X-factor and has single-handedly led the charge in the spin department. As for the pace department, it has been a collective effort, with Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib putting their hands up at different junctures in the competition. On the other hand, Nepal had history in their sights, with just 21 needed off 24 balls against South Africa and 7 wickets in hand. It wasn't to be, though, as they let it slip from a winning position and crumbled under pressure. Despite that loss, Nepal have shown that they are no pushovers and will aim to bow out on a high, possibly spoiling the party for Bangladesh. With one game against Sri Lanka being abandoned, Nepal have only had a couple of games to show what they got, and on the batting front, Rohit Paudel, Aasif Sheikh, and Anil Sah have displayed flashes of brilliance. Kushal Bhurtel and Dipendra Singh Airee may not have contributed with the bat as they would have liked, but the duo chipped in with the ball in the last game and formed a formidable spin attack alongside Sandeep Lamichhane. If Nepal are to take down Bangladesh, their pace contingent, consisting of Sompal Kami, Karan KC and Abinash Bohara, will have to come through. Rohit Paudel and Co. came ever so close to beating a Test-playing nation, South Africa, in the previous encounter. Can Nepal get the job done this time around and upset Bangladesh's apple cart? We will find out soon enough.
